tickers.reason: Scorpio Tankers — the PRODUCT-tanker expression of the freight trade, replacing the crude-tanker expression (FRO). Jul 16 2026 regime insight: the war escalated overnight (CENTCOM struck Qeshm/Bandar Abbas/Chabahar; Iran hit Ali Al Salem in Kuwait) and Brent FELL 0.37% to $84.63 — crude is flowing. Fuel is not. ~10% of global refining capacity (~8 Mbpd) is offline and the 3-2-1 crack hit an all-time-high ~$60-64.58/bbl. STNG is printing Q2-to-date TCE of $80,000/day on LR2s and $53,000/day on MRs (Q1 net income $216.3M), trading $78.11 with Strong Buy consensus and PT $89.83-$99.22. REPLACES FRO on RISK-ADJUSTED grounds, not conviction — this is a like-for-like freight swap that does NOT raise book correlation. FRO's VLCC thesis rests on ONE leg (Hormuz war-risk premium) that collapses the day a ceasefire is signed. STNG rests on TWO INDEPENDENT legs: (1) Iran/Hormuz route-lengthening AND (2) the refining deficit — Ukraine's drone campaign has disabled 42.74% of Russian refining capacity and Russia banned ALL diesel exports Jul 8-31 (Russia = ~11% of global diesel), forcing Turkey/Brazil/Africa/Mideast buyers onto US Gulf and Indian barrels and structurally lengthening clean ton-miles. Leg 2 is entirely independent of Tehran and survives de-escalation. CATALYST: Q2 2026 earnings early August (Q1 was May 5). Iran Sensitivity HIGH. RISK NOTED: 1-yr MR time-charter rates are only ~$19,500/day vs ~$50k spot — the forward curve does NOT believe the spike persists; this is a spot-rate trade, size accordingly.

Iran Sensitivity MEDIUM-HIGH (works on munitions-restock structurally, accelerates on escalation).

Hull war-risk premiums have repriced to a new-norm ~5% of vessel value (~$10-14M per VLCC voyage, up ~8x pre-conflict); London insurers report a hard, sticky specialty market as the June MoU collapsed in under three weeks. Iran Sensitivity HIGH (marine war-risk pricing is directly tied to Hormuz disruption). Two-way risk noted: an actual large tanker loss is a claims event, not only premium upside.

THE de-escalation-resilient conflict play: 3-2-1 crack spread holding ~$40/bbl even as Brent fell to ~$97 — refiners WIN on cheaper feedstock if Hormuz reopens while product premiums persist (capacity closures + distillate tightness). Replaces STNG to cut tanker double-weight (DHT+STNG) as de-escalation risk rose materially: oil down ~20% from 2026 peak, Lebanon ceasefire, Trump 60-day Hormuz MOU framework.
